definitions.explanation: The imaginary line around the middle of the Earth, equidistant from the North and South Poles, dividing the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.

examples.japanese: {赤道|せきどう}⟦{付近|ふきん}→付近：00044_fukin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{暑|あつ}い→暑い：00619_atsui⟧。
{赤道|せきどう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{越|こ}えると→超える：01942_koeru⟧⟦{南半球|みなみはんきゅう}→南半球：19054_minamihankyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When you cross the equator, you enter the Southern Hemisphere.

examples.japanese: ⟦エクアドル→エクアドル：noentry⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{赤道|せきどう}⟦{直下|ちょっか}→直下：noentry⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{国|くに}→国：02204_kuni⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Ecuador is a country directly on the equator.

examples.japanese: {赤道|せきどう}⟦{付近|ふきん}→付近：00044_fukin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{一年中|いちねんじゅう}→一年中：17104_ichinenjuu⟧⟦{気温|きおん}→気温：00235_kion⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: Near the equator, temperatures are high all year round.

examples.japanese: {赤道|せきどう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地球|ちきゅう}→地球：03461_chikyuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{北半球|きたはんきゅう}→北半球：20906_kitahankyuu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{南半球|みなみはんきゅう}→南半球：19054_minamihankyuu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}ける→分ける：02333_wakeru⟧⟦{線|せん}→線：09901_sen⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The equator is the line that divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

notes:
The {赤道|せきどう} is the line of 0° latitude that circles the Earth at its widest point. The name literally means 'red path' (⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ = red, ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧ = road/path).

GEOGRAPHICAL TERMS:
- ⟦{北半球|きたはんきゅう}→北半球：20906_kitahankyuu⟧: Northern Hemisphere
- ⟦{南半球|みなみはんきゅう}→南半球：19054_minamihankyuu⟧: Southern Hemisphere
- ⟦{北緯|ほくい}→北緯：noentry⟧: north latitude
- ⟦{南緯|なんい}→南緯：noentry⟧: south latitude
- {赤道|せきどう}⟦{直下|ちょっか}→直下：noentry⟧: directly on/under the equator

CLIMATE ZONES:
- ⟦{熱帯|ねったい}→熱帯：03531_nettai⟧: tropical zone (near the equator)
- ⟦{温帯|おんたい}→温帯：04479_ontai⟧: temperate zone
- ⟦{寒帯|かんたい}→寒帯：04124_kantai⟧: frigid zone (polar regions)
